title: Function Documentation
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of function documentation and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply naming functions clearly in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Function Documentation is part of Functions and Reusable Programming. Start with naming functions clearly and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Functions make behavior reusable; clear arguments, scope and return values make that behavior testable.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Functions make behavior reusable; clear arguments, scope and return values make that behavior testable. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Naming Functions Clearly
items.text: Use naming functions clearly to make input, output and scope explicit, then test both a typical call and one edge case.

items.title: Documenting Arguments
items.text: Use documenting arguments to make input, output and scope explicit, then test both a typical call and one edge case.

items.title: Explaining Return Values
items.text: Use explaining return values to make input, output and scope explicit, then test both a typical call and one edge case.

items.title: Documenting Errors and Side Effects
items.text: For documenting errors and side effects, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

items.title: Examples and Usage Notes
items.text: Explain examples and usage notes in the context of function documentation, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Call the function with typical, empty and invalid inputs, and inspect what it returns. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Function Documentation
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 72: Function Documentation
add_offset <- function(x, offset = 4) x + offset
add_offset(3)

content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Make inputs and return values explicit; also test an empty or invalid argument. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For function documentation, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply function documentation to a small synthetic example. Start with naming functions clearly, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the naming functions clearly idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.
content.expected_output: A reproducible function documentation example or design sketch with the expected result, one checked edge or failure case, and a stated limitation.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
